clue.text: It hangs with not so much at back

indicators.note: at back says the run of words before it is read from the end to the start

parts.note: not so much means less

explanation.surface: Something dangles, rather sparse at the rear, like a thinning tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole run 'not so much at', not just the word 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative tuft of threads is a hanging ornament on cushions, curtains and caps.

clue.text: Entrance, using commercial with sex appeal

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, AD for short
IT is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: An advertiser lures customers in by using sex to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A mining term: a horizontal passage giving access into a mine, so a way in.

clue.text: Moments of truth for downhearted performances

indicators.note: for links the down-at-the-heart to the performances it sits inside, the -hearted half saying where it goes

parts.note: performances on stage are shows
read as 'down-hearted': the word down, set at the heart of what follows

explanation.surface: Decisive moments arrive for actors giving dispirited performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downhearted' looks like gloom, but split in two it gives a word and, through its '-hearted' half, says where in the performances it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Final confrontations settle matters, which is when the truth of a situation comes out.

clue.text: Go before Doctor Daniel

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient named Daniel is told to go ahead of the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce or precede something is to open the way into it, coming first.

clue.text: Where strain results in parting

parts.note: sounds like emotional strain splitting people, but means the weakest component of a chain snapping under tension

explanation.definitionFit: A chain breaks at its feeblest component when tension is applied, so that is where it parts.

clue.text: What a government needs is most people off the dole

definitions.meaning: a governing party needs enough seats over the others to pass its business
read literally, the greater number of people being in jobs rather than claiming benefit (the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit)

explanation.surface: A government needs most people in jobs and not claiming unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary margin large enough to govern effectively; literally, a majority who are employed.

clue.text: Self-banking type of aircraft?

parts.note: auto- is the prefix meaning self
GIRO is a system of bank transfers, used in Britain for payments

explanation.surface: An aircraft that tilts itself into turns, banking without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' looks like an aircraft tilting in a turn, but it gives a bank-transfer system.
explanation.definitionFit: An early rotorcraft with an unpowered rotor and a propeller, a forerunner of the helicopter.

clue.text: Fast? Perhaps not!

parts.note: fast can mean firmly fixed, so something not fast is free and slack; also, a 'fast' woman is a promiscuous one, another sense of the same word

explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly fixed is fast; its opposite is slack or unfastened, which this word means.

clue.text: Dark suit appropriate in these places of entertainment?

parts.note: dark hours are night
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A dark suit is the right clothing for these evening venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Late-opening venues offering dancing, drinks and shows are places people go to be entertained.

clue.text: Is around? That's odd, as it disappeared a long time ago

definitions.text: it disappeared a long time ago

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so these letters are set in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something is still around, which is strange, since it supposedly vanished long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric reptiles that became extinct many millions of years ago are the classic thing long vanished.

clue.text: In depression, find somewhere to drink

definitions.meaning: a low point or hollow, as in an economic dip or a low-pressure area
a long open container from which animals drink

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low goes looking for a place to have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a low hollow or dip and the long container from which livestock drink water.

clue.text: They get passed on the road

definitions.text: They get passed on the road

parts.words: They get passed on the road
parts.note: seems to describe vehicles overtaken, but means examinations that learner motorists succeed in out on the road

explanation.definitionFit: Learner motorists sit practical examinations on public roads, and successful candidates have passed them.

clue.text: Kind of dance to be found in South Carolina or West Virginia?

definitions.text: Kind of dance to be found in South Carolina or West Virginia?

parts.words: Kind of dance to be found in South Carolina or West Virginia?
parts.note: a lively 1920s dance named after a city in South Carolina; West Virginia's capital has the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A 1920s jazz-age dance, named after the South Carolina port city; West Virginia's capital shares the name.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: a Chinese breed with a thick coat and blue-black tongue
informal word for grub or nosh

explanation.definitionFit: Both the name of a fluffy Chinese dog breed and a slang term for food.

clue.text: An outstanding feature of medieval architecture

definitions.text: An outstanding feature of medieval architecture

parts.words: An outstanding feature of medieval architecture
parts.note: outstanding means remarkable, but literally it means jutting out from the wall, as a grotesque carved waterspout does

explanation.definitionFit: Grotesque carved stone waterspouts project from the walls of medieval churches, literally standing out.

clue.text: With which one suffers a lack of balance

definitions.text: With which one suffers a lack of balance

parts.words: With which one suffers a lack of balance
parts.note: seems to be about unsteadiness on one's feet, but means a bank balance that has gone below zero

explanation.definitionFit: Drawing more money than the account holds leaves the customer with no credit balance at all.

clue.text: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Copenhagen?

definitions.text: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Copenhagen?

parts.words: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Copenhagen?
parts.note: at the Battle of Copenhagen in 1801 Admiral Nelson is said to have put his telescope to his sightless eye so as not to see a signal to withdraw

explanation.definitionFit: Nelson ignored an order by holding his telescope to his sightless eye; deliberate ignoring is named after it.

clue.text: Blair's going out on first-class return to acquire foreign capital

indicators.note: going out suggests leaving the original order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, taken as letters

indicators.note: return means the first-class pair is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Tony Blair leaves on a premium flight home to buy into a foreign capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' and 'return' read as Blair travelling but signal the shuffle and the turnaround. First-class is A1, the digit read as the letter I; the answer uses the Portuguese spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The purpose-built city that has been Brazil's seat of government since 1960.

clue.text: Expert returns to Mediterranean island

indicators.note: returns tells us to read the word for expert from back to front

parts.note: an expert is able, skilled

explanation.surface: A specialist goes back to a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian isle off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled in 1814.

clue.text: He'll tell us when it's over

definitions.text: He'll tell us when it's over

parts.words: He'll tell us when it's over
parts.note: seems to mean whoever announces the end, but in cricket an over is a set of six balls, and the official on the field calls it

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the match official calls 'over' after each set of six deliveries.

clue.text: Being knowledgeable, remind fellow that is distracted

indicators.note: distracted means confused or pulled about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A know-all reminds an absent-minded colleague of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has a great deal of knowledge is well-read and up to date.

clue.text: Girl needing daily refreshment

indicators.note: refreshment read as re-freshening, making something anew, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A young woman needs a drink or snack every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshment' looks like a drink but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in Lydia Bennet from Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Start the game and win

definitions.meaning: in shooting, ... strike the undergrowth to rouse birds into flight, so to start (flush out) the game

explanation.definitionFit: To flush out quarry by striking bushes, and to defeat someone in a contest.

clue.text: Indigestible food, for example Dorothy's turnover

indicators.note: a turnover flips something, so the words before are read backwards

parts.note: for example is abbreviated EG
Dot is short for Dorothy, so Dorothy's is DOTS

explanation.surface: Dorothy's apple turnover, a heavy pastry, is an example of hard-to-digest food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry but turns EGDOTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, starchy food that sits in the stomach is the classic indigestible fare.

clue.text: Copies I need to revise at times

indicators.note: to revise is to alter or rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student copies things out because they need to revise now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic or reproduce the behaviour of another is to copy them.

clue.text: Any in let out, naturally

indicators.note: out means wrong or not in its usual place, so these letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Anyone allowed in is naturally then let out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by inborn disposition happens by nature, without being learned.

clue.text: Executor's first to divulge what's left in the will

indicators.note: first means take just the opening letter of the word for executor

parts.note: to divulge is to state or declare

explanation.surface: An executor is the first to reveal what a will leaves to its heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: The total property and possessions a dead person leaves behind, distributed by the will.
